podcast.body: Co-written by Gram Parsons and Chris Hillman, this song from "Gilded Palace of Sin" explores the dark underbelly of Hollywood and reflects the transitional period between the 1960s and 1970s. It features a verse that references Bobby Kennedy's assassination in Los Angeles on June 6, 1968. "Written in 1969 as a 60s are becoming the 70s. It's about the darker side of Hollywood."

podcast.body: This song was mentioned by Robert Hilburn in a 1975 review, where he compared its themes of materialism and city life to The Eagles' "Lyin' Eyes." "lion eyes reminded him of sin city by the flying burrito brothers they are both songwriters they are both songs in their own ways about materialism."
